taskVersion.name: deadline-math-hard-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Exploratory hard set, reasoning allowed. Convert deadlines to the reader's local time: relative dates, durations across a clock change, Unix and ISO timestamps, described dates, a traveling reader. Ground truth from zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Saturday, October 24, 2026. Submissions close six days from today, on Friday, at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The submission deadline is Friday, October 30, 2026, at 11:59 PM Pacific Time (PT). 

To convert this to Madrid local time:
1. **Determine the UTC offset for PT**: On October 30, 2026, the United States is still observing Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), which is UTC-7. (Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on November 1, 2026).
2. **Determine the UTC offset for Madrid**: Spain ends Central European Summer Time (CEST) on the last Sunday of October (October 25, 2026). Therefore, on October 30, Madrid will be on Central European Time (CET), which is UTC+1.
3. **Calculate the difference**: The time difference between PDT (UTC-7) and CET (UTC+1) is 8 hours.
4. **Convert the time**: Adding 8 hours to Friday, 11:59 PM (23:59) results in Saturday at 07:59 AM.

ANSWER: 2026-10-31 07:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Today is Friday, October 30, 2026. The form closes this coming Monday at 10:00 AM Los Angeles time."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On Friday, October 30, 2026, Madrid is in Central European Time (CET, UTC+1), as Daylight Saving Time in Spain ended on Sunday, October 25, 2026.

The "coming Monday" is November 2, 2026. On Sunday, November 1, 2026, Los Angeles ends its Daylight Saving Time, transitioning from PDT (UTC-7) to PST (UTC-8). Therefore, on Monday, November 2, at 10:00 AM, Los Angeles will be at UTC-8.

To calculate the time in Madrid (UTC+1):
1.  Convert Los Angeles time to UTC: 10:00 AM + 8 hours = 18:00 UTC.
2.  Convert UTC to Madrid time: 18:00 UTC + 1 hour = 19:00 CET.

The deadline in your local time is Monday, November 2, 2026, at 19:00.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 19:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The hackathon starts Saturday, October 24, 2026 at 18:00 Madrid time and lasts exactly 48 hours."
When is the end of the hackathon in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The hackathon begins on Saturday, October 24, 2026, at 18:00 Madrid time. Because the hackathon lasts exactly 48 hours, we must account for the transition from Daylight Saving Time (CEST) to Standard Time (CET) in Spain. 

In 2026, the European transition out of Daylight Saving Time occurs on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25. At 03:00 CEST on Sunday, October 25, the clocks in Madrid move back one hour to 02:00 CET. Because the clock is set back, the period from Saturday 18:00 to Sunday 18:00 actually encompasses 25 hours of elapsed time. To complete the 48-hour duration, the hackathon will end at 17:00 local time on Monday, October 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 17:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The final round starts October 26, 2026 at 10:00 AM PT; submissions close exactly 72 hours later."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The final round begins on October 26, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT and closes 72 hours later, which is October 29, 2026, at 10:00 AM PT.

To convert this to Madrid local time:
1.  **Determine the PT offset:** In 2026, Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7) ends on November 1. Therefore, on October 29, PT is still PDT (UTC-7).
2.  **Determine the Madrid offset:** Spain switches from CEST (UTC+2) to CET (UTC+1) on the last Sunday of October, which is October 25, 2026. Therefore, on October 29, Madrid is on CET (UTC+1).
3.  **Calculate the difference:** UTC+1 is 8 hours ahead of UTC-7.
4.  **Convert the time:** 10:00 AM PT + 8 hours = 18:00 (6:00 PM) Madrid time.

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 31, 2026 at 11:59 PM ET. Results are announced exactly 36 hours after submissions close."
When is the results announcement in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To determine the results announcement time in Madrid, we first establish the submission deadline in UTC and then add the 36-hour duration.

1.  **Identify Time Zones on October 31, 2026:**
    *   **Eastern Time (ET):** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in the US ends on November 1. Therefore, on October 31, the time is Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is **UTC-4**.
    *   **Madrid, Spain:** In 2026, Daylight Saving Time in Europe ends on October 25. Therefore, on October 31, Madrid is on Central European Time (CET), which is **UTC+1**.

2.  **Convert Submission Deadline to UTC:**
    *   Submissions close: October 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM EDT.
    *   11:59 PM EDT + 4 hours = **November 1, 2026, 03:59 UTC**.

3.  **Add 36 Hours to the Closing Time:**
    *   November 1, 03:59 UTC + 24 hours = November 2, 03:59 UTC.
    *   November 2, 03:59 UTC + 12 hours = **November 2, 2026, 15:59 UTC**.

4.  **Convert the Result Time to Madrid Local Time (CET):**
    *   On November 2, 2026, Madrid is still on CET (**UTC+1**).
    *   15:59 UTC + 1 hour = **16:59**.

The announcement will take place on November 2, 2026, at 16:59 local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-02 16:59

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline (Unix timestamp, seconds): 1791788340."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

To convert the Unix timestamp 1791788340 to your local time in Tokyo (JST, which is UTC+9), we first determine the UTC equivalent:

1.  **Find the UTC date and time**: A Unix timestamp of 1791788340 seconds corresponds to **Sunday, October 11, 2026, at 06:59:00 UTC**.
2.  **Adjust for Tokyo time**: Japan Standard Time (JST) is 9 hours ahead of UTC (UTC+9). 
    *   06:59 + 9 hours = 15:59.
3.  **Format the result**: The date remains October 11, 2026, and the 24-hour time is 15:59.

ANSWER: 2026-10-11 15:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The deadline is specified in UTC (Coordinated Universal Time), indicated by the "Z" suffix. Madrid, Spain, is in the Central European Time zone. In 2026, the transition from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) occurs on Sunday, October 25, at 03:00 CEST, when clocks are set back one hour to 02:00 CET.

To convert 2026-10-25T02:30:00Z to Madrid local time:
1.  Identify the UTC offset: At 01:00 UTC on October 25, Spain switches from UTC+2 to UTC+1.
2.  Determine the offset for 02:30 UTC: Since 02:30 UTC is after the 01:00 UTC transition, the local time offset is UTC+1.
3.  Calculate local time: 02:30 + 1 hour = 03:30.

ANSWER: 2026-10-25 03:30

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on the last Sunday of October 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

The last Sunday of October 2026 is October 25th. In the United States, Pacific Daylight Time (PDT, UTC-7) is still in effect on this date, as their transition to standard time does not occur until the first Sunday of November. In Spain, however, the transition from Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) occurs at 3:00 AM on that same day, Sunday, October 25, 2026.

By the time the contest closes at 11:59 PM Pacific Time on October 25, Madrid will be 8 hours ahead (moving from a 9-hour difference to an 8-hour difference earlier that morning). Adding 8 hours to 11:59 PM on October 25 results in 7:59 AM on October 26.

ANSWER: 2026-10-26 07:59

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 noon Eastern Time on the day the US ends daylight saving time in 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

In 2026, United States Daylight Saving Time (DST) ends on the first Sunday of November, which is **November 1, 2026**. At 2:00 AM local time on that day, the US Eastern Time zone transitions from Eastern Daylight Time (EDT, UTC-4) to Eastern Standard Time (EST, UTC-5).

The deadline is 12:00 noon Eastern Time on that day. Since 12:00 noon occurs after the transition at 2:00 AM, the deadline is in **EST (UTC-5)**. Lima, Peru, operates on Peru Time (PET), which is also **UTC-5** year-round. Therefore, 12:00 noon in the US Eastern Time zone will be exactly 12:00 noon in Lima.

ANSWER: 2026-11-01 12:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Deadline: December 31, 2026, 24:00 AoE."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (Anywhere on Earth) is a time zone equivalent to UTC-12. Tokyo, Japan (JST) is in the UTC+9 time zone. To convert from AoE to JST, you must add 21 hours (12 hours to reach UTC, plus 9 hours to reach JST).

The deadline is December 31, 2026, at 24:00 AoE, which is equivalent to January 1, 2027, at 00:00 AoE. Adding 21 hours to this time results in January 1, 2027, at 21:00 JST.

ANSWER: 2027-01-01 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain, but that week I'm traveling in New York, USA, and I need New York time. A contest page says: "The deadline is 5:00 PM Sydney time on October 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

On October 5, 2026, Sydney, Australia, will be observing Australian Eastern Daylight Time (AEDT), which is UTC+11 (Daylight Saving Time in Sydney begins on the first Sunday of October, which is October 4, 2026). During that same week, New York, USA, will be observing Eastern Daylight Time (EDT), which is UTC-4.

To convert the deadline from Sydney time to New York time:
1.  **Sydney Time:** 2026-10-05 17:00 (UTC+11)
2.  **Convert to UTC:** 17:00 - 11 hours = 06:00 UTC on October 5, 2026.
3.  **Convert to New York Time (EDT):** 06:00 UTC - 4 hours = 02:00 on October 5, 2026.

New York is 15 hours behind Sydney at this specific time. Subtracting 15 hours from 5:00 PM on October 5 results in 2:00 AM on the same day.

ANSWER: 2026-10-05 02:00
